question: Two trains are moving in the same direction at 60 km/h and 42 km/h. The faster train crosses a man in the slower train in 36 seconds. Find the length of the faster train.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** in same direction = 60 − 42 = 18 km/h.

Convert to m/s: 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s.

**Length of faster train** = Relative Speed × Time = 5 × 36 = 180 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 180 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of **faster train** (S₁) = 60 km/h

Speed of **slower train** (S₂) = 42 km/h

**Time taken** (t) = 36 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4bd76160731c87a64db1c940305f8998fd376be54dcd0ce2958515d58164de45.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 60 − 42 = 18 km/h

⇒ Speed in m/s = 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s

⇒ Length of faster train = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ Length = 5 × 36

⇒ Length = 180 m

**∴ The correct answer is 180 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is (S₁ − S₂). When they move in **opposite directions**, relative speed is (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by **5/18**. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by **18/5**.

Crossing a Man vs. Crossing a Train

When a train crosses a **man**, the distance covered is the **length of the train** itself. If crossing another train completely, distance is the **sum of both lengths**.</p
